objectives.statement: Explain the concept of a limit as the value a function approaches near a point.
Evaluate limits graphically, numerically, and analytically including one-sided and infinite limits.
Determine where a function is continuous and classify discontinuities as removable, jump, or infinite.
Explain the derivative as instantaneous rate of change and the slope of the tangent line.
Apply power, product, quotient, and chain rules to differentiate functions.
Use implicit differentiation and solve related-rates problems.
Explain how the first and second derivatives reveal increasing/decreasing behavior and concavity.
Locate extrema and points of inflection and justify them with derivative tests.
Solve optimization problems and apply the Mean Value Theorem.
Explain accumulation and the definite integral as a limit of Riemann sums.
Evaluate definite and indefinite integrals using antiderivatives and u-substitution.
Apply both parts of the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.
Explain how integrals accumulate area and volume from cross-sections.
Calculate areas between curves and volumes of solids of revolution using disk, washer, and shell methods.
Explain what a differential equation and its general solution represent, including slope fields.
Solve separable differential equations and interpret the particular solution in context.
